headline: Approved Policy 500 on open enrollment, adding annual reporting and non-discrimination language; confirmed two coaches.
summary: The meeting covered the Check & Connect dropout-prevention program, the Rundlett Middle School construction project, transportation problems, the HB 1300 property tax cap, and staffing shortages. Policy 500 on open enrollment was approved with amendments on annual reporting and non-discrimination language.

Approved Amendment #1 requiring an annual summary report on open enrollment; motion carried.
Approved Amendment #2 adding non-discrimination language to Policy 500; motion carried.
Approved Policy 500, Open Enrollment, as amended; motion carried unanimously by voice vote.

Board of Education Minutes – October 5, 2026 
 
Board members present: Pamela Walsh – President, Cara Meeker – Vice President, Liz Boucher – 
Secretary, Jess Campbell, Alex Dubois, Brenda Hastings, Barb Higgins, Madeleine Mineau, and Sarah 
Sadowski 
 
Administrators/Staff: Timothy Herbert – Superintendent, Matt Cashman, Jack Dunn, Bridget Edinger, 
Kris Gallo, Kaily Roukey 
 
Call to Order 
Ms. Walsh called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM and asked Ms. Boucher to take roll call attendance. 
 
Consent Agenda 
a. Special BOE Meeting (August 26) 
b. Regular Monthly Meeting (September 1) 
c. Special BOE Meeting September 14) 
d. Executive Committee (September 21) 
e. Finance Committee (September 21) 
f. City & Community Relations (September 23) 
The Board voted 9-0, via vice vote, to approve the Consent Agenda (Moved by Ms. Boucher, 2nd by 
Ms. Higgins). 
Discussion 
• Ms. Sadowski requested a correction to the minutes of the Special BOE Meeting on September 
14th, changing the term "non dormatory" to "non-discriminatory." 
• Discussion occurred regarding City and Community Relations Committee minutes and 
clarification that the minutes included were from August 17 rather than September 23. Staff 
indicated follow-up would occur regarding the September 23rd. 
On a voice vote, the Board voted 9-0 to approve the consent agenda as amended. 
Superintendent Timothy Herbert introduced new student board representative Tabitha Chapman, a 
junior at Concord High School and student in the CRTC Cosmetology II program. 
Tabitha Chapman shared remarks regarding her commitment to student advocacy and serving 
alongside the existing student representative. 
School Celebration Presentation
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – October 5, 2026 
 
Principal Richard introduced Fern Seiden, Director of Staff and Student Wellness, and Ashley Lavery, 
Check & Connect Mentor, who presented an overview of the Check & Connect Program. The 
presentation highlighted the research-based mentoring model developed by the University of 
Minnesota. Th program focuses on dropout prevention, attendance and engagement monitoring, 
family involvement, student mentoring, and data-informed interventions. Presenters reviewed the 
implementation of the program at Rundlett Middle School and Concord High School, shared student 
success stories and testimonials, and discussed the program's funding through the Project AWARE 
grant. 
 
Board members discussed the program's impact on students' social-emotional growth and 
relationship-building, the use of student performance data to increase self-awareness and 
accountability, long-term sustainability of the program, and the return on investment provided 
through grant funding. The Board also discussed the reasons for selecting the Check & Connect model 
over other intervention programs and expressed appreciation for the positive outcomes being 
observed among participating students. 
 
Recognitions & Reports 
Student Representative Clementine Mayala shared the PSAT testing schedule for Freshmen, 
Sophomores, and Juniors. Clementine also shared upcoming events as well as the Homecoming 
football victory over Central High School.  
 
Tabitha Chapman shared some student concerns around restoring a late bus for CHS students and 
additional support and resources for seniors completing college applications.  
 
Superintendent Herbert provided an update on transportation operations and ongoing challenges 
across the district. He discussed potential grant opportunities that may support the restoration of a 
late bus program and reviewed the district's recent bus stop consolidations. The Superintendent also 
addressed winter safety concerns related to bus stop locations, ongoing communication with families 
regarding transportation issues, and staffing challenges resulting from bus driver shortages. In 
addition, he reviewed several transportation safety concerns that have been raised throughout the 
district and outlined efforts to address them. 
The Superintendent reported a minor bus accident involving contact with a parked vehicle's mirror. An 
insurance claim has been filed. 
The Superintendent reported successful attendance at the Open Houses and positive community 
participation across district schools. 
Dr. Herbert reported that the Rundlett Middle School Groundbreaking Ceremony was a successful 
event with strong participation from community members, school board members, contractors, 
project partners, and representatives from organizations involved in the middle school construction 
project. He highlighted the performance by the Rundlett Middle School choir and thanked the staff 
and facilities team for their work in organizing the event. Dr. Herbert also provided an update on the 
progress of the middle school construction project and expressed appreciation to everyone who 
contributed to the success of the ceremony.
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – October 5, 2026 
 
 
An instructional tutor position has been posted to support two sections at Abbot Downing School. 
Applications have been received and are under review. 
Superintendent Herbert provided an overview of HB 1300, recently enacted state legislation that 
establishes a property tax cap and places limitations on central office administrative spending. He 
reviewed the impact the law could have on Concord and Merrimack Valley school districts, including 
ballot questions that will appear before voters and concerns regarding the potential for residents in 
one district to vote on tax-cap measures affecting another district. The Superintendent also informed 
the Board that legal counsel is conducting additional analysis of the legislation and its potential 
implications for the district. 
Administration presented an update on increasing student services needs and ongoing staffing 
challenges across the district. The discussion focused on growing demands for special education 
services, the impact of students with significant support needs moving into the district, staffing 
shortages, and a vacancy in occupational therapy services. Administrators reviewed how these 
staffing challenges are affecting school operations and noted potential budget implications associated 
with meeting required student supports. 
 
Administration reported an identified need for 19 additional educational assistant positions; however, 
the reassignment of three vacant positions reduced the immediate need to 16 positions. Additional 
occupational therapy staffing needs are also being evaluated. Board members discussed the fiscal 
impact of these requests, the district’s legal responsibilities under the Individuals with Disabilities 
Education Act (IDEA), obligations related to charter school and foster placement services, and 
potential future budget adjustments needed to address the growing demand for services. 
 
Capital Facilities 
Mr. Cashman provided an update on the Rundlett Middle School construction project, reporting 
continued progress in several areas of work. He reviewed the status of geothermal well installation, 
foundation construction, masonry work, and utility infrastructure improvements. Mr. Cashman noted 
that the project remains on schedule and outlined upcoming milestones, including the presentation of 
the Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) for the project at a future Capital Facilities and Building 
Committee meeting. 
Traffic Study Review 
Rebecca Brown of GPI presented additional traffic circulation alternatives for the Rundlett Middle 
School project. She reviewed several options for parent and bus traffic routing, discussed the 
potential impacts on surrounding neighborhoods, and outlined associated sidewalk and pedestrian 
safety considerations. Ms. Brown also reviewed traffic-flow challenges and operational impacts of the 
proposed alternatives, noting that some options may warrant further evaluation or testing in the 
future if adjustments to traffic patterns are needed once the new school opens. 
Finance
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – October 5, 2026 
 
Mr. Dunn reviewed the district's financial report, including the status of salary and benefit accounts, 
professional services expenditures, transportation costs, utility budgets, workers' compensation 
adjustments, reserve fund activity, and supply budgets. He also provided an overview of current 
budget activity and areas that will continue to be monitored throughout the fiscal year. 
Board members asked questions regarding the district's workers' compensation funding, the 
availability of paper and classroom supplies, and the cost of contracted services. Administration 
explained the workers' compensation budget adjustment process, confirmed that adequate funding 
remains available for general classroom supplies, and reviewed the financial impact of contracted 
service costs compared to filling positions with district employees. Additional discussion focused on 
monitoring these expenses as the fiscal year progresses. 
Communications & Policy 
Ms. Meeker presented Policy 500 – Open Enrollment on 2nd reading. Discussion included feedback 
received during the public hearing, several proposed amendments related to reporting requirements, 
non-discrimination language, and application timelines, as well as technical and formatting revisions 
to the policy. Board members and administration discussed implementation considerations, state 
requirements, and the importance of monitoring the policy's impact as the district begins the open 
enrollment process. A vote will take place after Public Comment. 
City & Community Relations 
The City and Community Relations Committee provided an update on recent activities, including 
reflections on the Multicultural Festival and positive community feedback regarding district strengths, 
particularly the relationships among students, staff, and families. The committee also discussed 
transportation-related concerns and community engagement 
Public Comment 
Nancy Rhodes, a veteran educator and parent, spoke on behalf of her daughter, a former Beaver 
Meadow kindergarten teacher who resigned after being reassigned to a new school and grade level. 
She raised concerns about how the resignation was communicated and urged the district to better 
support early-career teachers and consider the impact of staffing changes on educators and students. 
 
Jessie Morency A parent of a child with disabilities and former educational assistant, Ms. Morency 
highlighted concerns about staffing and consistent support for students with significant needs. She 
encouraged stronger collaboration among families, educators, and administrators, emphasizing the 
important role parents can play in improving student outcomes. 
 
Lucas Gallo, a Concord parent, taxpayer, district employee, and community member, encouraged 
Board members to visit Mill Brook School to better understand the needs of students and staff. He 
highlighted the increasing complexity of student needs, the challenges faced by school personnel, and 
the dedication of staff members. Mr. Gallo suggested that firsthand observation would help inform 
future decisions regarding staffing, resources, and budgeting.
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – October 5, 2026 
 
Joey Daniels, a community member, encouraged the district to adopt a unified Concord identity by 
using Concord High School's crimson and white colors across youth sports, middle school athletics, 
and high school programs. He noted that many neighboring communities use consistent colors 
throughout their athletic programs, helping build school pride and community identity while 
potentially reducing costs for families. Mr. Daniels also shared that he submitted a petition with 283 
signatures supporting the proposal. 
 
Lindsay McGee, lead special education teacher of the OWL Program at Mill Brook School, shared 
concerns about ongoing staffing shortages affecting students with autism and other complex learning 
needs. She explained that her program is currently short two educational assistants, limiting her 
ability to provide instruction, support staff, complete evaluations, and fulfill other required 
responsibilities. Ms. McGee emphasized that while staff remain dedicated to supporting students, 
current staffing levels make it difficult to provide the level of service and support students deserve. 
 
Dr. Vicki Hopkins, an occupational therapist with 27 years of experience and 17 years in the Concord 
School District, spoke about the growing demands on occupational therapy services. She explained 
that occupational therapists support students with a wide range of educational, medical, and 
behavioral needs and that their responsibilities extend beyond direct services to include evaluations, 
family collaboration, and compliance activities. Dr. Hopkins emphasized that caseload numbers alone 
do not reflect actual workload and expressed support for increasing occupational therapy staffing to 
meet student needs. 
 
Personnel 
Superintendent Herbert presented two coaches for confirmation: 
 
• Grant Kelly, CHS Freshman Volleyball Coach 
• Katelynn Edwards, RMS Girls Soccer B2 Coach 
 
The Board, via voice vote, confirmed the coach nominations as presented (Moved by Ms. Higgins, 2nd 
by Ms. Mineau). 
 
Votes 
The Board voted via voice vote, to approve Policy 500, Open Enrollment upon 2nd reading (Moved by 
Ms. Meeker, 2nd by Ms. Higgins). 
The Board discussed several proposed amendments to Policy 500, including the addition of non-
discrimination language, application deadlines, annual reporting requirements, demographic data 
collection, and district reporting processes. Administration expressed concerns about extending the 
application deadline due to state reporting requirements, enrollment projections, and limited staffing 
availability during the summer months. 
Board members discussed the importance of monitoring the implementation of open enrollment, 
collecting data to assess potential impacts, and ensuring transparency throughout the application 
process. The Board reviewed reporting and demographic data collection requirements intended to 
help evaluate participation and outcomes while ensuring application decisions are made in
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – October 5, 2026 
 
accordance with district policy and state law. Following discussion, the Board approved amendments 
related to annual reporting and non-discrimination language before approving Policy 500 as 
amended. 
Amendment #1 - Annual Reporting Requirement 
Motion: Ms. Sadowski moved to amend Policy 500 to require the district to annually provide the 
Board with a summary report on the open enrollment process, including the number of applications 
received, sending districts, anonymized demographic information, reasons applicants sought 
enrollment, and acceptance and denial data. 
Second: Ms. Campbell. 
Vote: Motion carried. 
Motion: Ms. Campbell moved to amend Policy 500 to include non-discrimination language stating that 
the district shall not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender 
identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, genetic information, pregnancy, or 
any other characteristic protected by law. The amendment also requires that any demographic 
information collected during the open enrollment application process be clearly identified as not 
being used in admissions decisions and be accompanied by a statement of non-discrimination. 
Second: Ms. Sadowski. 
Board members discussed the importance of ensuring that demographic information collected 
through the application process is used only for data collection and reporting purposes and not as a 
factor in admission decisions. 
Vote: Motion carried. 
Final Vote on Policy 500 
Motion: Approve Policy 500, Open Enrollment, as amended. 
Vote: Motion carried unanimously by voice vote. 
The Board discussed the upcoming New Hampshire School Boards Association annual meeting. 
Members noted that the district had not submitted any resolutions this year. Board members 
interested in attending were asked to notify administration once the meeting date was confirmed. 
Other Business 
Superintendent Herbert reported that elementary enrollment is currently down by 21 students 
districtwide: 
• Abbott-Downing School: down 2 
• Beaver Meadow School: down 3 
• Broken Ground School: down 5
Monthly Board of Education Meeting – October 5, 2026 
 
• Christa McAuliffe School: down 1 
• Mill Brook School: down 10 
 
Dr. Herbert also noted that preschool and kindergarten enrollment figures typically fluctuate during 
the opening weeks of the school year due to age eligibility and enrollment timing. 
Administration reported several notable enrollment changes. The district has experienced an increase 
of 24 students identified as experiencing homelessness or living in transitional housing situations, 
noting that these numbers may continue to fluctuate as student status is reviewed and updated 
throughout the school year. Additionally, the Concord Regional Technical Center (CRTC) reported a 
decrease of 11 students in enrollment compared to prior figures.
